full_judgment:
This Rule, calls in question the legality and propriety of Judgment and decree dated 15-2-2001 passed by learned Subordinate Judge, Third Court, Naogaon, in Title Appeal No. 134 of 1991 allowing appeal and dismissing suit by reversing judgment and decree dated 6-5-1991 passed by learned Assistant Judge, Raninagar, decreeing Title Suit No. 35 of 1990 (analogously heard with Title Suit No. 34 of 1990). 

 6. On the pleadings different issues were settled including issue of maintainability and issue whether plaintiffs are entitled to get a decree as prayed for. 

 8. After hearing learned Judge of trial Court by judgment and decree dated 6-5-1991 decreed both suits. Against aforesaid judgment and decree passed in Other Class Suit No. 35 of 1990 defendant preferred Title Appeal No. 134 of 1991 in the Court of District Judge, Naogaon, which was ultimately heard by learned Sub-ordinate Judge, Third Court, Naogaon who by judgment and decree dated 15-2-2001 allowed the appeal and dismissed Title Suit No. 35 of 1990. No appeal was preferred against the judgment and decree passed in Other Class Suit No. 34 of 1990. 

 10. Feeling aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree petitioners preferred the instant application and obtained the present Rule. 

 11. Mr Harandra Nath Nandy, learned Advocate appearing with Mr Shahed Ali Jinnah, Advocate, for petitioners, seeks to impeach the impugned judgment and decree on two-fold arguments. Firstly, defendant is not entitled to get the land even the deeds are genuine because the same was done with a view to deprive the legal heirs of Khair Ali. In support of his contentions, learned Counsel refers the case of SM Brajabala or Brajabashi Saha, vs Tarapada Saha Minor, 11 DLR 40 wherein it has been held: 

 12. Secondly, the learned Judge of trial Court after considering materials on record rightly decreed the suits but the Court of appeal below without reversing finding of facts arrived at by trial Court allowed the appeal and dismissed the suits, thereby committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. 

 15. Now the question which calls for consideration, whether the Court of appeal below committed any error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in passing the impugned judgment and decree. 

 18. On appraisal of evidence of PW 1 Moijan Bibi I do not find any specific evidence that she did not put her left thumb impression in the register book and she also failed to show that her signature appears in the registered book is not her signature. Therefore, learned Judge of Court of appeal below as a final Court of facts came to a definite findings that deed of gift and Hebabil-Ewaz were executed by plaintiffs. I am in full agreement with the views of learned Judge of Court of appeal below. The trial Court without considering the materials on record, particularly transfer of land by deed of Aronnama in favour of plaintiffs, decreed both the suits which, in my view, are not correct. 

 22. Moreover, the impugned judgment and decree of Court of appeal below in its entirety are well founded in the facts and circumstances of the case. Therefore, the grounds urged and the contentions advanced by the learned Counsel for the petitioners are not the correct exposition of law. So, same stands rejected having been devoid of any substance. 

 23. In view of discussions made above and the preponderant judicial views emerging out of the authorities referred to above I am of the view that the impugned judgment and decree of the Court of appeal below suffers from no legal infirmity which calls for no interference by this Court. Thus the Rule having no merit fails. 

 24. In the result, the Rule is discharged without any order as to cost. The impugned judgment and decree dated 15-2-2001 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Third Court, Naogaon, in Title Appeal No. 134 of 1991 is hereby affirmed.
